native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via the gardening pathway varies systematically with habitat in the Barcelona province: it is highest in Wetlands, Urban and Coastal habitats (about 45-50% of plots contain at least one gardening-introduced species), intermediate in Riparian (~36%), and markedly lower (<=21%) in Croplands, Scrublands, Broad-leaved forests, Coniferous forests, Rock outcrops and Meadows. Within plots that are invaded, gardening is the dominant pathway (54-100% of invaded species) in Wetlands, Coastal, Coniferous forests and Broad-leaved forests, whereas in Croplands unintentional introductions dominate (~19% gardening, p_bonf=0.005). The habitat effect survives adjustment for elevation and urban/cropland landscape context (NB GLM: Wetlands IRR=6.16 p=0.002, Urban IRR=6.24 p=0.002, Coastal IRR=5.62 p=0.005, Riparian IRR=6.28 p=0.001 vs Broad-leaved forests; urban and cropland covariates non-significant at p>0.6). The dominant garden-origin taxa - Robinia pseudoacacia, Dysphania ambrosioides, Phytolacca americana, Lonicera japonica, Pittosporum tobira - are wide-niche horticultural species matching the high-prevalence habitats. Chi-square test of independence across the ten habitats is highly significant (chi2=75.20, df=18, Monte-Carlo p<2e-4 from 5000 permutations). Catalonia-wide, the gardening share of new introductions rose from 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985-2019. Phylogenetic-tree sensitivity: all 81 species in invasion_success_pathways.csv map to the supplied Newick tree, so the headline is not driven by phylogenetic-sampling gaps; the tree-anchored pathway mix (Gardening 42/81, share 0.519) equals the full pool.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded the four data files. Verified n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo == n.total for all 632 plots and that (lon,lat) pairs are unique. Grouped invaded_niche_pathways.csv by habitat and computed per-habitat sum_gard/sum_unint/sum_agfo/sum_total and plot_prev_gard = mean(n.gard>0) plus 95% bootstrap CIs (B=2000 stratified by habitat). Built a 10x3 contingency table; ran chi-square test plus 5000-permutation Monte-Carlo p. Ran pairwise 2x3 Fisher-exact tests with Monte-Carlo row-total fixed (B=2000) and Bonferroni correction across 10 habitats. Fitted a Negative-Binomial GLM n.gard ~ habitat + elevation + urban.2009.500m + cropland.2009.500m (statsmodels GLM with NB family); reference Broad-leaved forests; reported IRRs and p-values. Cross-referenced invasion_success_pathways.csv to rank the top-10 gardening species by combined rank of number.of.invaded.plots and area.of.occupancy.10km and labelled their ecological affinity from species traits (note: per-species habitat affiliation cannot be extracted from invaded_niche_pathways.csv because counts are aggregated across species). Verified phylogenetic coverage by regexing every label from the Newick tree including hyphenated names and intersecting with phylo.tip.label in invasion_success_pathways.csv (81/81 mappable). Used temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv to compute the gardening share per period as a one-line background context for the hypothesis.
